library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zitzmann_2026_bemnifosbuvir_ruzasvir"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zitzmann_2026_bemnifosbuvir_ruzasvir"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70454> (open access; PMC13541962)

Zitzmann et al. fitted a multiscale HCV viral-kinetic model to the HCV RNA
and ALT data of 215 treatment-adherent patients who took bemnifosbuvir (an
NS5B nucleotide polymerase inhibitor) 550 mg plus ruzasvir (an NS5A
inhibitor) 180 mg once daily for 8 weeks. There is no pharmacokinetic layer:
the combination is assumed to act with constant effectiveness from the start
of treatment, after a short pharmacological delay.

# Population

The analysis set is the per-protocol, treatment-adherent subset (215 of 275
enrolled) of the phase 2 single-arm trial NCT05904470 (Table 1 of the paper):
mean age 51 years (range 20-85), 46.5% male, 72.6% White and 20.5% Asian.
Genotype 1 accounted for 70.2% of patients, genotype 3 for 27.0%, genotypes 2
and 4 for 1.9% and 0.9%. Fibrosis stages were F0 22.8%, F1 27.9%, F2 23.7%,
F3 9.8% and compensated cirrhosis (F4) 15.8%. The HCV RNA assay had a lower
limit of quantification (LLOQ) of 15 IU/mL. SVR12 was 97.7% (210/215).

# Model structure

The multiscale model (S1_Text eq 1) tracks target cells, infected cells by
infection age, intracellular positive-strand HCV RNA within an infected cell,
and free virus. Assuming no new infections during treatment, the plasma viral
load has the analytic solution (S1_Text eq 2)

$$V(t) = V_0\left[C_1 e^{-c(t-\tau)} + C_2 e^{-(B+\delta)(t-\tau)} + C_3 e^{-(\gamma+\delta)(t-\tau)}\right], \quad t > \tau,$$

with $B = \rho(1-\varepsilon_s) + \kappa\mu$, $A_R = \alpha_R(1-\varepsilon_\alpha)$,
$N = \rho(\alpha_R+\delta)/[\delta(\rho+\mu+\delta)]$ and the coefficients
$C_1$, $C_2$, $C_3$ given in S1_Text. The three coefficients sum to 1, so
$V = V_0$ until the delay $\tau$ has elapsed. Serum ALT follows S1_Text eq 4,

$$A(t) = A_N\left(1 - \frac{A_0 - A_N}{A_N(c_A-\delta)}\left(\delta e^{-c_A t} - c_A e^{-\delta t}\right)\right), \quad A_N = s / c_A.$$

The packaged model evaluates both solutions directly; it has no ODE states.
Time is in days since the first dose. The outputs are `log10_viral_load`
(log10 IU/mL, as fitted) and `lnalt` (natural log of ALT in U/L; the paper
fitted log10 ALT, and the two differ only by the factor ln 10).

In the final model (B24) the drug blocks intracellular RNA production
($\varepsilon_\alpha$) and virion assembly/secretion ($\varepsilon_s$), and
multiplies the intracellular RNA degradation rate by $\kappa$; the
replication-complex decay $\gamma$ is fixed to 0. Compensated cirrhosis
(`DIS_CIRRHOSIS = 1`, fibrosis F4) shifts $\varepsilon_\alpha$ and
$\varepsilon_s$.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value in model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Viral-load solution $V(t)$, $C_1$-$C_3$, $N$, $A_R$, $B$ | `vl`, `c1_vl`, `c2_vl`, `c3_vl`, `n_ss`, `a_r`, `b_rna` | S1_Text eq 2 and the definitions below it |
| ALT solution $A(t)$, $A_N = s/c_A$ | `alt`, `alt_n` | S1_Text eq 4 |
| Phase durations $D_1$, $D_2$ (checked below) | computed in this article | S1_Text, after eq 2 |
| $V_0$ | `lrbase` = log(10^6.48) IU/mL | Table 3 (6.48 log10 IU/mL, RSE 0.79%) |
| $\delta$ | `ldelta` = log(0.269) /day | Table 2, model B24 (0.269); Table 3 rounds to 0.27 |
| $c$ | `lc` = log(19.62) /day | Table 3 |
| $\tau_v$ | `ltau` = log(1.8/24) day | Table 3 (1.8 h) |
| $\alpha_R$ | `lalpha_r` = log(40), fixed | Table 3; Methods |
| $\rho$ | `lrho` = log(8.18) /day, fixed | Table 3; Methods |
| $\mu$ | `lmu` = log(1) /day, fixed | Table 3; Methods |
| $\varepsilon_\alpha$ F0-F3 / F4 | `logiteps_alpha` = logit(0.9859); `e_dis_cirrhosis_eps_alpha` = logit(0.9935) - logit(0.9859) | Table 3; Table 2 B24; Table S5 B24 |
| $\varepsilon_s$ F0-F3 / F4 | `logiteps_s` = logit(0.9978); `e_dis_cirrhosis_eps_s` = logit(0.9904) - logit(0.9978) | Table 3; Table 2 B24; Table S5 B24 |
| $\kappa$ | `lkappa` = log(1.705) | Table S5 B24 (1.705); Table 3 rounds to 1.70 |
| $\gamma$ | `gamma_rc` = 0, fixed | Table 3; S1_Text (B24 fixes $\gamma$ = 0) |
| $s$ | `lkin_alt` = log(5.23) U/L/day | Table 3 |
| $c_A$ | `lkout_alt` = log(0.30) /day | Table 3 |
| $A_0$ | `lrbase_alt` = log(31.57) U/L | Table 3 |
| Between-subject variances | all `fixed(0)` | not reported (see Assumptions) |
| Residual SDs (log10 HCV RNA, log ALT) | `fixed(0)` | not reported (see Assumptions) |
| Individual parameters of the 215 patients | `data/Zitzmann_2026_individual_parameters.csv` | S2_Text individual-parameter table |

# Typical-value trajectories

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Zitzmann_2026_bemnifosbuvir_ruzasvir")

times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 1 / 48), seq(2, 56, by = 0.25))))
ev_typ <- tidyr::crossing(
  id = 1:2,
  time = times
) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, DIS_CIRRHOSIS = id - 1L)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_typ,
  omega = NA,
  sigma = NA,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(id == 1, "F0-F3", "F4 (compensated cirrhosis)"))
```

```{r fig2-vl, fig.cap = "Typical HCV RNA decline over the 8-week treatment, by fibrosis group. Compare with Figure 2a,c,d of Zitzmann 2026. Dotted lines: LLOQ (15 IU/mL) and the cure boundary (6.67e-4 IU/mL)."}
ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, log10_viral_load, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = log10(c(15, 6.67e-4)), linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(
    x = "Time since start of treatment (day)",
    y = "HCV RNA (log10 IU/mL)",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig2-early, fig.cap = "First two days of treatment: the delay of about 2 h, the rapid first phase (virion clearance) and the start of the second phase. Compare with Figure 2a of Zitzmann 2026."}
ggplot(filter(sim_typ, time <= 2), aes(time * 24, log10_viral_load, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Time since start of treatment (h)", y = "HCV RNA (log10 IU/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig2-alt, fig.cap = "Typical ALT trajectory. Compare with Figure 2b of Zitzmann 2026. ALT falls from A0 = 31.6 U/L towards the uninfected level s/c_A = 17.4 U/L."}
ggplot(filter(sim_typ, id == 1), aes(time, exp(lnalt))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5.23 / 0.30, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "Time since start of treatment (day)", y = "ALT (U/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Phase structure against the Results text

The Results section reports the phase rates and durations of the triphasic
decline. They follow from the typical parameters through the S1_Text
formulas $D_1 = \ln(C_1/C_2)/(c - B - \delta)$ and
$D_2 = \ln(C_2/C_3)/(B + \gamma)$.

```{r phases}
phase <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(group) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    second_phase_rate = kappa * mu + delta,
    D1_h = log(c1_vl / c2_vl) / (c - (b_rna + delta)) * 24,
    D2_h = log(c2_vl / c3_vl) / (b_rna + gamma) * 24
  )

# log10 decline attributed to each phase: the phase's exponential rate times
# its duration (first phase c, second phase B + delta)
phase <- phase |>
  mutate(
    drop1_log10 = c * D1_h / 24 / log(10),
    drop2_log10 = (b_rna + delta) * D2_h / 24 / log(10)
  )

phase_cmp <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Second-phase rate kappa*mu + delta (/day)",
    "First-phase duration D1, F0-F3 (h)", "First-phase duration D1, F4 (h)",
    "Second-phase duration D2, F0-F3 (h)", "Second-phase duration D2, F4 (h)",
    "First-phase decline, F0-F3 (log10)", "First-phase decline, F4 (log10)",
    "Second-phase decline, F0-F3 (log10)", "Second-phase decline, F4 (log10)"
  ),
  Packaged = c(
    phase$second_phase_rate[1],
    phase$D1_h, phase$D2_h,
    phase$drop1_log10, phase$drop2_log10
  ),
  Published = c(1.97, 8.4, 6.5, 36, 46, 3, 2.3, 1.3, 1.6)
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (Packaged - Published) / Published)

phase_cmp |>
  mutate(Packaged = signif(Packaged, 3), `Difference (%)` = round(`Difference (%)`, 1)) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(abs(phase_cmp$`Difference (%)`) < 10)
```

The second-phase rate and the phase durations agree with the Results text to
within the rounding of the printed parameters (the largest duration gap,
about 4% for the F4 first phase, comes from carrying the rounded Table 3
values). The per-phase declines are the phase's exponential rate times its
duration ($c D_1$ and $(B + \delta) D_2$, in log10 units), which reproduces
the paper's "3 log" vs "2.3 log" first-phase and "1.3" vs "1.6 log"
second-phase figures; the F4 second phase (1.72 vs 1.6 log10) is the widest
gap. The total drop from $V_0$ by the end of the first phase is smaller than
$c D_1$, because the second exponential already contributes during the first
phase.

# Replaying the 215 patients

The paper's time-to-undetectable analysis (Figure 4) simulated each patient
with their own estimated parameters. S2_Text tabulates those individual
estimates for all 215 patients; they are shipped with this article as
`data/Zitzmann_2026_individual_parameters.csv`. Because each patient's
$\varepsilon_\alpha$ and $\varepsilon_s$ already include the cirrhosis
effect, they enter the model through its population parameters with
`DIS_CIRRHOSIS = 0`.

```{r replay}
ind <- read.csv(file.path("data", "Zitzmann_2026_individual_parameters.csv"))
stopifnot(
  nrow(ind) == 215,
  sum(ind$fibrosis == "F4") == 34, # Table 1
  sum(ind$genotype == 1) == 151,
  sum(ind$genotype == 3) == 58
)
ind <- ind |>
  mutate(
    id = seq_len(n()),
    fib_group = ifelse(fibrosis == "F4", "F4", "F0-F3")
  )

params_ind <- ind |>
  transmute(
    id,
    lrbase = log(10^log10V0),
    ldelta = log(delta),
    lc = log(c),
    ltau = log(tau),
    logiteps_alpha = qlogis(eps_alpha),
    logiteps_s = qlogis(eps_s),
    lkappa = log(kappa),
    lkin_alt = log(s),
    lkout_alt = log(cA),
    lrbase_alt = log(A0)
  )

ev_ind <- tidyr::crossing(id = ind$id, time = seq(0, 84, by = 0.05)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, DIS_CIRRHOSIS = 0L)

sim_ind <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  params = params_ind,
  events = ev_ind,
  omega = NA,
  sigma = NA,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  left_join(select(ind, id, genotype, fib_group), by = "id")

# Each patient's solution starts at their own V0
stopifnot(max(abs(sim_ind$log10_viral_load[sim_ind$time == 0] - ind$log10V0)) < 1e-8)
```

## Early decline

```{r early}
early <- sim_ind |>
  filter(round(time, 6) %in% c(0.25, 0.5, 1)) |>
  left_join(select(ind, id, log10V0), by = "id") |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(mean_decline = mean(log10V0 - log10_viral_load), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    hours = time * 24,
    published = c(1.4, 2.9, 3.3)
  )
early |>
  select(`Time (h)` = hours, `Mean decline, packaged (log10)` = mean_decline,
    `Mean decline, published (log10)` = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(abs(early$mean_decline - early$published) < 0.3)
```

The paper reports mean reductions of 1.4, 2.9 and 3.3 log10 at 6, 12 and
24 h (Results); the replay gives the values above.

## Time to undetectable HCV RNA and to the cure boundary

```{r tte}
first_crossing <- function(time, y, threshold) {
  i <- which(y <= threshold)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) Inf else time[i]
}

tte <- sim_ind |>
  group_by(id, genotype, fib_group) |>
  summarise(
    t_lloq = first_crossing(time, log10_viral_load, log10(15)),
    t_cure = first_crossing(time, log10_viral_load, log10(6.67e-4)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summ <- function(d, label) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Group = label,
    n = nrow(d),
    t_lloq = median(d$t_lloq),
    t_cure_wk = median(d$t_cure) / 7
  )
}
tte_tab <- bind_rows(
  summ(tte, "All"),
  summ(filter(tte, genotype == 1), "GT 1"),
  summ(filter(tte, genotype == 3), "GT 3"),
  summ(filter(tte, fib_group == "F0-F3"), "F0-F3"),
  summ(filter(tte, fib_group == "F4"), "F4")
) |>
  mutate(
    t_lloq_pub = c(11.4, 13.0, 8.6, 11.0, 15.6),
    t_cure_pub = c(6.6, 7.0, 5.6, 6.5, 6.9),
    lloq_diff = 100 * (t_lloq - t_lloq_pub) / t_lloq_pub,
    cure_diff = 100 * (t_cure_wk - t_cure_pub) / t_cure_pub
  )

tte_tab |>
  transmute(
    Group, n,
    `Median days to LLOQ, packaged` = t_lloq,
    `Median days to LLOQ, published` = t_lloq_pub,
    `Difference (%)` = lloq_diff,
    `Median weeks to cure boundary, packaged` = t_cure_wk,
    `Median weeks to cure boundary, published` = t_cure_pub,
    `Difference (%) ` = cure_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1))

stopifnot(
  abs(tte_tab$lloq_diff) < 5,
  abs(tte_tab$cure_diff) < 12
)
```

The medians of the time to the LLOQ match the published Figure 4 values to
within 1%. The time to the cure boundary (6.67e-4 IU/mL) agrees overall and
for the F0-F3 group; for GT 1 and F4 the replay is 0.35-0.6 weeks later than
the text. The cure boundary sits more than nine log10 below baseline, so it
depends on each patient's slow third phase ($\delta$), and the S2_Text table
prints $\delta$ to three decimals; the gap is in that tail, not in the model
structure, which the LLOQ times confirm.

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Percentage of patients with HCV RNA at or below the LLOQ (15 IU/mL), by genotype and by fibrosis group, from the replay of the 215 patients. Compare with Figure 4b,c of Zitzmann 2026."}
km <- bind_rows(
  tte |> filter(genotype %in% c(1, 3)) |> mutate(panel = "Genotype", strata = paste("GT", genotype)),
  tte |> mutate(panel = "Fibrosis group", strata = fib_group)
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(day = seq(0, 56, by = 0.25)) |>
  group_by(panel, strata, day) |>
  summarise(pct = 100 * mean(t_lloq <= day), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(km, aes(day, pct, colour = strata)) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(x = "Time since start of treatment (day)", y = "Patients <= LLOQ (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Virologic response rates

```{r response}
resp <- tibble::tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "vRVR (<= LLOQ by day 7), all", "vRVR, GT 3",
    "RVR (<= LLOQ by week 4), all", "RVR, F4",
    "<= LLOQ by week 6, all"
  ),
  Packaged = c(
    sum(tte$t_lloq <= 7),
    sum(tte$t_lloq[tte$genotype == 3] <= 7),
    sum(tte$t_lloq <= 28),
    sum(tte$t_lloq[tte$fib_group == "F4"] <= 28),
    sum(tte$t_lloq <= 42)
  ),
  Denominator = c(215, 58, 215, 34, 215),
  Published = c(57, 22, 205, 28, 214)
)
knitr::kable(resp)
stopifnot(all(abs(resp$Packaged - resp$Published) <= 2))
```

The replay reproduces the paper's response counts: vRVR 57/215 (26.5%) and
22/58 in GT 3, RVR 205/215 (95.3%) and 28/34 in F4, and all patients but one
(a patient with cirrhosis) at or below the LLOQ by week 6.

## Viral decline relative to baseline by subgroup

```{r fig2-subgroups, fig.cap = "Median (line) and 10th-90th percentile band of the change in log10 HCV RNA from baseline over the replayed patients, by fibrosis group and by genotype. Compare with Figure 2d,e of Zitzmann 2026."}
rel <- sim_ind |>
  filter(time <= 56, abs(time / 0.5 - round(time / 0.5)) < 1e-6) |>
  left_join(select(ind, id, log10V0), by = "id") |>
  mutate(dlog = log10_viral_load - log10V0)

rel_band <- bind_rows(
  rel |> mutate(panel = "Fibrosis group", strata = fib_group),
  rel |> filter(genotype %in% c(1, 3)) |> mutate(panel = "Genotype", strata = paste("GT", genotype))
) |>
  group_by(panel, strata, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(dlog),
    lo = quantile(dlog, 0.1),
    hi = quantile(dlog, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(rel_band, aes(time, med, colour = strata, fill = strata)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(x = "Time since start of treatment (day)", y = "Change in HCV RNA (log10)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Why there is no NCA

The model has no pharmacokinetic component: the drug effect is a constant
effectiveness switched on after the delay $\tau$. Noncompartmental analysis
of drug concentrations therefore does not apply, and the paper reports no NCA
parameters. Validation instead rests on the closed-form phase structure, the
early decline, and the patient-level replay of the published time-to-event
and response results above.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Between-subject variability and residual error are not reported.** The
  paper gives the fixed effects (Table 3) but no random-effect variances or
  residual-error SDs. The S2_Text individual estimates differ between patients
  on all ten estimated parameters, so the model carries an eta on each, fixed
  to 0, and fixes both additive residual SDs to 0. Stochastic simulation from
  the packaged model is therefore typical-value only; the subgroup
  variability shown above comes from the published individual estimates.
* **Parameter transforms.** The paper does not state the Monolix
  distributions. The model uses logit-normal $\varepsilon_\alpha$ and
  $\varepsilon_s$ (both constrained to (0, 1) in the paper) with the
  cirrhosis effect as a shift on the logit scale, which is how Monolix
  applies a categorical covariate to a logit-normal parameter, and
  log-normal distributions elsewhere. $\kappa$ is constrained to be at least 1
  in the paper; the log-normal form here does not enforce that bound, which
  matters only if variability is added. With all etas fixed to 0 the
  transforms do not change any simulation.
* **Rounded values.** Where the paper prints a parameter at two precisions,
  the more precise one is used: $\delta$ = 0.269 /day (Table 2, B24; Table 3
  gives 0.27) and $\kappa$ = 1.705 (Table S5; Table 3 gives 1.70). The
  pharmacological delay is 1.8 h (Table 3), carried as 0.075 day.
* **ALT unit and scale.** Table 3 prints the unit of $s$ as IU/L; in S1_Text
  eq 3 it is a production rate, so it is carried in U/L/day. The paper fitted
  log10 ALT; the packaged output `lnalt` is the natural log, which differs by
  the constant factor ln 10. The ALT solution (S1_Text eq 4) has no delay
  term, and none is added.
* **Time origin and scope.** Time 0 is the first dose and the drug effect is
  constant afterwards. The analytic solution describes the on-treatment
  decline only; it does not model the end of treatment, viral rebound or
  relapse, and it assumes no new infections during treatment.
* **Covariate scope.** Compensated cirrhosis (F4 vs F0-F3) on
  $\varepsilon_\alpha$ and $\varepsilon_s$ is the only covariate in the final
  model. Genotype (GT 1-4), individual fibrosis stages (F0-F4) and the
  F0-F2 vs F3-F4 grouping were screened (Tables S2-S7) but not retained.
* **Replay inputs.** The individual parameters were transcribed from the
  S2_Text table, which prints them to 2-4 significant figures, and the time
  grid of the replay is 0.05 day (1.2 h), so crossing times are resolved to
  that grid.
